explanation: After taking Babylon he let deported peoples, including the Jews, return home. His tomb, a stone chamber on a stepped base, survives at Pasargadae in Iran.

claims.text: Cyrus the Great founded the Persian (Achaemenid) Empire in the 500s BC and conquered Babylon in 539 BC.
The Assyrian Empire fell in the late 600s BC, Cyrus overthrew the Median kingdom, and the Hittite Empire had collapsed around 1200 BC.
Cyrus allowed peoples exiled to Babylon, including the Jews, to return to their homelands.
The tomb of Cyrus, a stone chamber on a stepped plinth, stands at Pasargadae in Iran.
